inputs.text: This is being sold as a transparency push, but it looks more like outside institutions helping shape the Dominican Republic’s rules—and calling that “integrity.” On 25 March 2026 in Paris, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader watching. The polished anti-corruption language is useful cover: whoever gets to define the standards also gets influence over how the country is governed.
